PROPOSED LEGISLATION TARGETS TRANSLOCATOR DUMPING

Heliastes, WSJ Editor-in-Chief

   Responsible tunnel excavators and miners often pack their mining tailings into crates for future processing into various building materials. However, a growing problem has arisen for many local towns: Amateur miners following get-rich-quick dreams simply digging out the minerals they seek and simply dumping the stones into the nearest translocator available.
   "It's an absolute disaster!" exclaimed Azrielle, Western regions mountain pass maintainer. "I rode my elk to our local West Elk Corridor entrance, and while we were stepping onto the translocator, I just heard a loud crashing sound. When I came to, I was buried in thousands of granite stones with my elk. I couldn't move a muscle!" It took rescue workers over 8 hours to remove enough stones to extract Azrielle and their elk. Both suffered numerous bone fractures and spent months in rehab.
   "It's a huge problem because a small group of irresponsible miners is casting a shadow on the entire mining industry," said Nudge, representative of the Highway & Tunnel Workers Union. "Why should the whole sector suffer harsher regulations because of the actions of a few bad actors?" Small mom & pop miners disagree. "It's Big Dig that forces us to cut costs like this," said Valian094, an 'opportunistic miner' who seeks out unlocked mineshafts for leftover ores. "Big Dig claims all the good deposits and blocks off all the surface entrances, forcing us to mine in from the sides and scavenge what we can from the edges of the claims. We don't have the time to get in and out with all the stones, so we just find a TL nearby and dump all the tailings." Valian094 shrugged, "Who cares; out of sight, out of mind."
   Lawmakers, eager to pass new regulations requiring permits for mining activity of any sort, are facing major hurdles advancing the legislation. "All these lawmakers do is add more hoops to jump through before you can get any honest work done," said Fialova, member of the TOPS Individualist Society. "They all seem to forget that what makes TOPS great is the people; people digging the earth, people farming the crops, people depleting the countryside of every damn bear in sight. Dave bless the people!"

RUST CONTAGION "WIPEALL" CULLS LIVESTOCK, WIDESPREAD PANIC

Heliastes, WSJ Editor-in-Chief

   A previously unknown contagion has spread rapidly across TOPS, virtually obliterating all livestock it has come into contact with. Scientists have codenamed the contagion "Wipeall" but so far have not provided any details into the origin or nature of the contagion. "It's unlike anything we've ever seen before," said lilyniru, researcher at TOPS University. "It seems to spread along social interactions but the behavior of the contagion doesn't resemble that of any disease we've yet discovered."
   So far, tens of thousands of livestock, including chickens, pigs, sheep, and even elk, have been destroyed by the virus, leaving no trace of the victims. "It's like they just disappeared into thin air, right in front of my eyes!" said Koidatfish, heavily bandaged around their head. "I was riding my elk and, all a sudden, he just vaporized right under me! I fell like 5 feet, face-first, into the pavement at 20 bps; doctor says it'll be months before they know how much I'll recover my handsome good looks." So far, no seraphs have been reported to be affected by the contagion. However, due to the nature of the instant vaporization of victims, any seraphs affected may not be reported until missing persons reports can be verified. Some reports have also surfaced of objects such as boats being disintegrated; why such objects would be affected by the contagion is still unclear at time of this reporting.
   Panic broke out among the general population before martial law was declared late this afternoon. Residents gathered around Spawn for a "TOPSy Turvy Armageddon" celebration of the perceived End Times. Kralmir, head of the agra-conglomerate Kralmir Feed & Seed was witnessed throwing crates worth of cabbage out into the masses. "Nothing matters anymore," exclaimed Kralmir to the masses, "My life is a waste! All my rusty gears can't come with me to Dave's Island in the Sky!" He then ripped off all his clothes and ran out screaming into the wilderness. Others burned wordly possessions in a massive bonfire, forsaking their materialistic desires and begging forgiveness from Dave for all their hubris. "I've strayed from the path Dave has set out for me, said Purx, famed outlaw. "All things from Dave, and to Dave all things!" Purx then threw their gold gear, crystal skull, mianguan, and other collectibles into the flames, before cramming a fistful of liberty caps into their mouth then convulsing on the floor in a hallucinogenic stupor.

by Stuvals, Master Tailor & Diplomat of
the Barony of Westwald

I once was a man with hopes... aspirations, and
dreams. Now, I am but a shell. The horrors I
witnessed have scarred me beyond repair. This
is my tale. This... is my story. 

Wandering southward in search of a new life
I went, bringing nothing but the clothes on my
back and a boyish ambition to homestead in a 
green wonderland. But then... once I had reached 1,000 blocks in that direction, something ocurred. 

The clouds begun fading into a putrid moldy hue. When the rain from above hit me... it stun my
skin. Suddenly, a circular totalitarian statue towered above me and the eyes of a fox painted
onto a sign leered at me. "VAK'S" it said.

I continued, with great hesitation, onwards. I 
neared ever closer to what appeared to be a
fenced-in complex. The clanks and clinging of
pickaxes, the groans of overworked men, they'd
jolt when the acid rain hit them... but never would
they utter a noise... why?

"SPEAK ONLY WHEN SPOKEN TO!" screamed
a brash superintendant. The workers trembled in
fear. It horrified me to realize that even the rocks
they were mining were oozing with green sludge.
A strike of thunder rang through the horizon, 
providing me with a slight glimpse of what was
laid before me. 

Endless rows of chests. Endless signs. Endless
crates... all filled to the brim. "BUY NOW!" a sign
said. "50% OFF!" another read. I felt intense 
sorrow seeing the sight of it. 

ZAP! I turned. Lightening? No... far worse. An
employee attempting to escape had triggered 
the electric fence keeping them all contained. His
body slid into a muddy ditch, a small grin shown
on his face. Finally free from his misery... content
in the warm embrace of death.

"Hello!" a warm kindrid voice said. I glanced to 
my right. Then to my left. "Up here, friend!"
Looking above me I saw an innocent gentleman
sitting upon a tree branch. It was the only tree
in the vacinity. Dead, rotten to the core. 

"Would you like some food?" the unknown 
gentleman bellowed. 

I clenched my jaw. "I... I certainly wouldn't mind,
I'm quite pekish," I said.


"Surely you wouldn't, pal!" He reached into his
pocket and threw me a loaf of bread. "Say...
you seem to be new. Where ya goin'?" 

I take a few bites of the loaf. Charred flax bread.
"South, I'm new here. I intend to farm... maybe
raise some animals."

"Well, some new tools certainly wouldn't do you
any harm, would it?" 

My eyes can't help but look back at the apalling
sight before me... but I must tell you, dear reader:
Man is made of flesh and blood... and desire. 
My dreams, in this very moment, overpowered
any misgiving I may have toward this endeavor. 
Stupid as I was. Naive... oh God... how naive. I
shall never forgive myself. 


I was new. My belly was for the first time no
longer aching for food. And a person who seemed
as innocent as a dog offered me all I've ever 
wanted. A clean start. A fresh one, free from the
dangers of starvation. Perhaps I should've 
recalled... he's no dog- but a fox. 

Returning to the conversation, "Tools would be
nice, yes, thank you! I assume you'd wish for
something in return...?"

"Of course, but you can leave whenever 
you'd like!" The gentleman said, reaching to
shake my hand with a bright smile. "Vak, Vak
is my name. I'd ask for your name... but I have a
new one for you. Employee #62." 

He then threw me a "uniform". An orange jumpsuit
with an "EMPLOYEE #62" tag attached.

The lapel was sharp, digging straight through the
thin garment and into my chest, hurting me each
time I moved. The superintendant came over and
Vak vanished. A few of the workers coughed...
but no usual "clearing your throat" cough. It 
sounded as if their lungs were filled with mucus.

"NUMBER #62, YOU ARE TASKED WITH 
RETRIEVAL OF VAK'S PROPERTY. YOU
SHALL TAKE THIS COPPER PICKAXE AND
DIG DOWNWARDS AT YOUR DIRECTED SPOT
UNTIL YOU REACH IT." She said with a fury.

"...what, what-" I stutter. "What is this property
exactly?" 

She huffed. "EMPLOYEE #62, YOU ARE NOT
TO ASK QUESTIONS. HERE, NOW," she led me
to a small pit. "DIG DOWN!"

And so... I obeyed. I dug deeper and deeper. 
Disgusting green mulch sometimes submerged
the pit. Hours went by, days? I no longer recall.
It stank... horribly. I gagged and tried to hold my
collar over my nose. 

A dark orange color appeared out of the toxic
waste. "An ore? Perhaps this is valuable, maybe
I really can leave here with new tools," I thought
to myself. As I continued to dig... I saw more
emerge from the stinking depths. 

A finger... its nails encrusted with grime. Frantically, I dug faster. Gasping, "H- HELP!" 
Pausing. "I FOUND SOMEONE! HE- HE 
DOESN'T LOOK SO GOOD!" 

The superintendant leans her head over the hole.
It appears only as a small pixel above me.

"EMPLOYEE #62, THAT IS VAK'S PROPERTY.
RETRIEVE IT AND RETURN TO SURFACE-
LEVEL. NOW." She blares, her voice echoing
down to me. 

Tears fill my eyes. I slowly removed the earth
covering the corpse. "Wh- w... why? Property?
This is a man!" I shriek at the top of my lungs. 

"GUARDS!" the superintendant yelps. Immediately I'm peppered with arrows, piercing
my back as I crouch for safety within the pit. 
"CONTINUE YOUR WORK, EMPLOYEE #62
WITHOUT EMOTION!" 

Blood trickles down my stained orange jumpsuit. 
I crawl upwards, tugging the corpse along with me. On the back of his jumpsuit it reads: 
"EMPLOYEE #61". 

"I'll- I'll get you out of here!" I whisper crazily to
the body. "I'll... I'll get us out of here."

Upon reaching the surface, the superintendant
stands with her arms crossed. "YOU WILL
RECEIVE MEDICAL ATTENTION AFTER YOUR
TASK. DIG A GRAVE."

Wiping tears off my face I dig. "THROW 
VAK'S PROPERTY, EMPLOYEE #61 IN THERE
NOW." I obey. I... I obey. She walks over and 
sticks a dirt tombstone above it, and writes with
chalk upon it: "EMPLOYEE #61, 22 VAKBUCKS
EARNED."

Is that all a man is to these people? His assigned
number and value added to the corporation? 
These... these were people. With names, families.
Hopes... dreams, just the same as I!

How could life and dignity be assaulted more? 
It... it couldn't be. My face soured. I ran, I- I 
just simply ran. My overworn workshoes slowly
came apart as my feet continued pounding the
slimey pavement. 

I tore off my lapel and unzipped my jumpsuit as
I ran for my life. Arrows pelted me. Boars, dogs
were released from their kennels and sprang
upon me. Each time I managed to dodge their
howling fangs with what little energy I had left.

"STOP HIM. EMPLOYEE #62 IS TRYING TO 
ESCAPE!" I heard from behind. After some-time
of bolting I arrived at the electric fence... "I 
don't care... I don't care how bad this hurts!" I
manically screamed. "I SHALL BE ONLY ONE
THING: A FREE MAN!"


The electrical current ran up and down my veins
with nigh unquantifiable speed. But it didn't 
matter, for Employee #61's spririt was with me
even if my own had left me. 

I... I escaped. Morning came, I don't even 
remember when. How long was I pursued? 
How long have I been running? Was this
just purely a nightmare? No... no no no. It was
real.

If from the comfort of my office in Westwald I
forget Employee #61, his death would be in vein.
I will not allow that, so I now put this tale into 
writing... it's all I have left in my now fractured
mind.

BEARTOWN NEAR BANKRUPTCY

Heliastes, WSJ Editor-in-Chief

   Beartown is quickly running out of capital to fund its daily operations, leaving residents worried about the future of the town. The reason: excessive auction house listings, upwards of 10,000 total, leading to exorbitant deposit fees. Combined with low sales volume, compounding debt interest, and a rapidly aging population, the result is a massive drain on the town's coffers.
   "I'm so distraught, I don't even know what to do," said AliceMargatroid, town resident and food inspector. "I barely have a job anymore; I go to inspect the food quality in the granary and all I find is rot because no ones paid for rodent extermination. It feels like the entire town is rotting from the inside out!
   Yoma22k, town mayor and architect of the auction house scheme, begged to differ. "Auction house listings do more than just bring in capital through sales; it also gets word out positive publicity about Beartown as a commerce leader." When asked about why so many listings were necessary, Yoma22k replied, "It's all about saturating the market. People can't buy what they don't see. No visibility, no sales."
   Other auction house vendors opposed this point of view. "If this strategy is so great, how come Beartown is struggling to pay the bills and how come there's virtually no sales?" asked dirtgrubs, a tradesperson specializing in dirt and termites. "The worst part is that these listings hurt everyone by spamming so many listings you can't find what you want." dirtgrubs then demonstrated by taking a bunch of acorns on top of a parchment, then slapping animal fat on top of it. "See, if you want acorns but there's all this spam on top, you can't get to it!" dirtgrubs then threw the fat-smeared parchment at Yoma22k's warehouse before stomping off, leaving it caked onto the wall.

WIPEISM 2ND MOST PREVALENT RELIGION

Heliastes, WSJ Editor-in-Chief

   It's official; no longer is Wipeism relegated to fringe shamans and doomday cultists. In recent years, this once niche belief system has developed into a full-fledged, codified religion with an organized caste of priests and attendants. "There's a cold comfort in knowing it will all eventually end," said Marabunta12, avid acolyte of the Western Church of the Final Wipe. "Everyone says that the world has begun anew and nothing will happen soon, but recent events only show that everything and everyone we know can disappear in an instant." Marabunta12 then pointed to a memorial plaque commemorating all the elks lost in the Wipeall Plague.
   TOPS University studies show that Wipeism has quickly caught up to Daveism, the dominant religion in TOPS, with nearly 30% of Vintagians expressing some level of adherence. Wipeists are attracted to the deterministic consequences of the perceived incoming wipe, allowing them to accept the inevitable and live their lives fully without restraint. 

           TOPS Residents By Religion
                                 Daveism --------------| 54%
                                 Wipeism ------| 29%
Obligate Anarcho-Capitalists --| 11%
            Constantinopleopians -| 6%
                                                     Source: TOPS U.

   "It's still a cult, no matter how popular it becomes," said JadexDead, priest at the West Ocean Temple of Dave. "Unlike Daveists, who clearly have a basis for our belief in a giant giraffe-like monster that wanders the earth during storms, driving seraphs mad and destroying anything that inspires its wrath, Wipeists just roll over and give up in the face of something that isn't even guaranteed to happen." JadexDead added, "Just because it happened once, doesn't mean it'll ever happen again. Probably. Maybe..." JadexDead then stared out across the ocean, ever so slightly releasing their grasp on their Dave scepter.

I clenched my jaw. "I... I certainly wouldn't mind, I'm quite pekish," I said.


"Surely you wouldn't, pal!" He reached into his pocket and threw me a loaf of bread. "Say... you seem to be new. Where ya goin'?"

I take a few bites of the loaf. Charred flax bread. "South, I'm new here. I intend to farm... maybe raise some animals."

"Well, some new tools certainly wouldn't do you any harm, would it?"

My eyes can't help but look back at the appalling sight before me... but I must tell you, dear reader: Man is made of flesh and blood... and desire. My dreams, in this very moment, overpowered any misgiving I may have toward this endeavor. Stupid as I was. Naive... oh God... how naive. I shall never forgive myself.


I was new. My body was for the first time no longer aching for food. And a person who seemed as innocent as a dog offered me all I've ever wanted. A clean start. A fresh one, free from the dangers of starvation. Perhaps I should've recalled... he's no dog- but a fox.

Returning to the conversation, "Tools would be nice, yes, thank you. I assume you'd wish for something in return...?"

"Of course, but you can leave whenever you'd like!" The gentleman said, reaching to shake my hand with a bright smile. "Vak, Vak is my name. I'd ask for your name... but I have a new one for you. Employee #62."

He then threw me a "uniform". An orange jumpsuit with an "EMPLOYEE #62" tag attached.

The lapel was sharp, digging straight through the thin garment and into my chest, hurting me each time I moved. The superintendent came over and Vak vanished. A few of the workers coughed... but no usual "clearing your throat" cough. It sounded as if their lungs were filled with mucus.

"NUMBER #62. YOU ARE TASKED WITH RETRIEVAL OF VAK'S PROPERTY. YOU SHALL TAKE THIS COPPER PICKAXE AND DIG DOWNWARDS AT YOUR DIRECTED SPOT UNTIL YOU REACH IT." She said with a fury.

"...what, what" I stutter. "What is this property exactly?"

She huffed. "EMPLOYEE #62, YOU ARE NOT TO ASK QUESTIONS. HERE, NOW," she led me to a small pit. "DIG DOWN!" 

And so... I obeyed. I dug deeper and deeper. Disgusting green mulch sometimes submerged the pit. Hours went by, days? I no longer recall. It stank... horribly. I gagged and tried to hold my collar over my nose.

A dark orange color appeared out of the toxic waste. "An ore? Perhaps this is valuable, maybe I really can leave here with new tools," I thought to myself. As I continued to dig... I saw more emerge from the sinking depths.

A finger... its nails encrusted with grime. Frantically, I dug faster. Gasping, "H- HELP!" Pausing. "I FOUND SOMEONE! HE- HE DOESN'T LOOK SO GOOD!"

The superintendent leans her head over the hole. It appears only as a small pixel above me.

"EMPLOYEE #62, THAT IS VAK'S PROPERTY. RETRIEVE IT AND RETURN TO SURFACE- LEVEL. NOW." She blares, her voice echoing down to me.

Tears fill my eyes. I slowly removed the earth covering the corpse. "Wh- w... why? Property? This is a man!" I shriek at the top of my lungs.

"GUARDS!" the superintendent yelps. Immediately I'm peppered by arrows, piercing my back as I couch for safety within the pit. "CONTINUE YOUR WORK, EMPLOYEE #62 WITHOUT EMOTION!"

Blood trickles down my stained orange jumpsuit. I crawl upwards, tugging the corpse along with me. On the back of his jumpsuit it reads. "EMPLOYEE #61".

"I'll- I'll get you out of here!" I whisper crazily to the body. "I'll... I'll get us out of here."

Upon reaching the surface, the superintendent stands with her arms crossed. "YOU WILL RECEIVE MEDICAL ATTENTION AFTER YOUR TASK. DIG A GRAVE."

Wiping tears off my face I dig. "THROW VAK'S PROPERTY, EMPLOYEE #61 IN THERE NOW." I obey. I... I obey. She walks over and sticks a dirt tombstone above it, and writes with chalk upon it: "EMPLOYEE #61, 22 VAKBUCKS EARNED".

Is that all a man is to these people? His assigned number and value added to the corporation? These... these were people. With names, families. Hopes... dreams, just the same as I.


How could life and dignity be assaulted more? It... It couldn't be. My face soured. I ran, I just simply ran. My overworn workshops slowly came apart as my feet continued pounding the slimy pavement.

I tore of my lapel and unzipped my jumpsuit as I ran for my life. Arrows pelted me. Boars, dogs were released from their kennels and sprang upon me. Each time I managed to dodge their howling fangs with what little energy I had left.

"STOP HIM. EMPLOYEE #62 IS TRYING TO ESCAPE!" I heard from behind. After some time of bolting I arrived at the electric fence... "I don't care... I don't care how bad this hurts!" I manically screamed. "I SHALL BE ONLY ONE THING: A FREE MAN!"


The electrical current ran up and down my veins with nigh unquantifiable speed. But it didn't matter, for Employee #61's spirit was with me even if my own had left.

I... I escaped. Morning came, I don't even remember when. How long was I pursued? How long have I been running? Was this just purely a nightmare? No... no no no. It was real.

If from the comfort of my office in Westwald I forget Employee #61, his death would be in vein. I will not allow that, so I now put this tale into writing... it's all I have left in my now fractured mind.

attrs.text:
by Stuvals, Master Tailor & Diplomat of the 
Barony of Westwald

I had intended to write this great work of mine
regarding a glorious and successful expedition
to the far north yet... fate had other plans in mind.
No, no. It would be evil to speak of my
accomplishments when I had discovered 
something far more horrifying! 

It all begun when I had the dream of discovering
an icy pole, to be the first to reach the furthest
expanse ever seen by man. My fellow countrymen
in Westwald called me insane. They mocked me
openly in the tavern at that! "That uppity burgher!" our farmer sneered. But none of this
deterred me. I would be the first man to conquer
the north!


As I packed my dear elk, Blitzer, I felt an intense 
sting of anxiety. "Am I truly an uppity burgher? A
man too big for his little wooden shoes? NO!" I
yelped. At that very moment I began flying
upon the western highway toward spawn to
find glory, riches, and fame... oh, if only I had known what I do now. 

Choosing to depart in Summer, I passed by vast
fields of green as far as the eye can see. Berries
grew. Peasants hassled me for food as I passed. No matter! I gave them nothing, no charity! How could I? I must conserve all I can for
my trek north! My toupée flapped in the brisk wind. 

But then, I arrived. At... Perch Point? Where have
the people gone? The streets were bare, absolutely empty. "What?" I thought. 

The town appeared very different than prior trips... A lone man, his hands upon his head. Slumped along a street corner, he rasped to me, "He is gone... Leviticus... I was his tailor..." 

"Whom is this? Tell me now, beggar!" I blared,
adjusting my fake hair to appear dignified. 

"Our leader... our... savior, he has not returned...
nor has the population... 'tis only I... me... the
former tailor..." the man managed to choke
out of his dehydrated throat. 

For a moment I could only reflect upon this horrid
sight. Perch Point without people? This was a 
boom town. The very same town that had aided
our great Baron in his time of need! It is
Perch Point we westerners owe our respect! How
could this happen? Where is their leader? 

"WHERE HAVE THEY GONE, MAD BEGGAR?"
I asked, my anger boiling. "WHERE ARE THEY,
THESE GREAT INDUSTRIOUS PEOPLE?" I 
paused, pointing toward their windmill, "IT STILL
SPINS, DOES IT NOT?" 

The man merely fell over. His face smudged
in charcoal with his cheekbones stuck out in
hunger. 

"BEGGAR!" I screamed. "BEGGAR?!" Immediately I rushed toward the nearest pond to give him water, throwing a bucketful on his face. He didn't wake. What has happened here? How
can oh so many people disappear?

"An odd tale, one told by a lost man. Full of falsehoods at that! It will not effect me or my expedition!" I proclaimed. 

After that incident I arrived at "spawn" and careened Blitzer northward upon the rustic highway. I noticed quickly he had trouble walking across such harsh ground. "Those roadworkers in Throughway..." I muttered to myself, now realizing the highway turns into a one-by-one tunnel into some useless mountain.

All was well and jolly. My food provisions were
high and my spirits remained unbroken by the mad fainting peasant. "How could Perch Point
ever die?" I jokingly asked myself. It couldn't, that
was the answer I came to. 

...but then, I came upon a mysterious sight roughly thirty-thousand blocks north. A campfire.
With... a note! A knife had pinned it to a collapsed
tree, the paper fluttered in the wind as it clung to the log. 

"It's year three and we have gone the furthest
north! There's ten of us now... if our tailor hadn't
turned back in fear it would be eleven. How 
foolish of him. Anyways, hello from Perch Point!"

- Leviticus

Interesting... I put the note in my breast-pocket. 
That madman was truly apart of this expedition.
"Perhaps the wholesome people of Perch Point
had found a better home... it is quite swampy in
that lake of theirs," I said to myself, resting and
moving Blitzer onwards soon after.

The days passed slower and soon... night became nonexistent. I reached fifty thousand blocks north and crossed massive ice formations, navigable with only a pickaxe. I put on my
snow goggles to prevent snow-blinding. 

I rode past polar bears and arctic foxes competing
for limited game. Their weight all low, all starving
in such terrifying conditions. Zero settlements. 
I had chosen to keep to the middle of the map, 
knowing that if I zig-zagged too much I may get
lost.

But then, a brownish smudge appeared in the 
pitch-white horizon. I thought I was crazy until
Blitzer, huffing in the cold air, approached it. A 
sign! "LEVITICUS OF PERCHPOINT, 50K" it
stated. "They've made it far, with ten people
nonetheless!" I thought to myself. 

A "day" (if you could call it that) went on. Blitzer
trudged through the glacier ice until a new biome
appeared. Along a shabby dirt road a new 
sight came into view. A pair of trousers? 


I stepped off my elk and inspected them. They
were full of needles, poor knitting. A ways further
a blue shirt bleached in the sun. Then... a cave. 
Inside it was red writing upon the wall, 

"S A V E   U S !   L E V I T I C U S   H A D
P R E S S E D   ON !   W E   A R E   T O O 
S I C K   F R O M   D I S E A S E   T O
C O N T I N U E !"

My nose was flushed with a stench. A putrid and
rotting one. "OH, GOD!" I gasped. A mountain of
eight skeletons were tucked into the cave, within 
their pots were limbs. "CANNIBALISM!" I blared 
with horror, running out. 

Now... dear reader, let us be honest, would we not eventually do the same in these poor, poor
Perchpointers shoes? 

Imagine, you trek onwards for months... perhaps
years without provisions. Would you not resort
to their states if you too were diseased from scurvy and malnutrition? 

I would. I chose, and still do as of writing this to
not judge them. They were, when I knew them,
a good people... that is how I still remember their
great town. Do not allow my writing to change your views due to their plight.

My morale for the expedition was shot yet I kept
pushing past the sad... sad sights I'd seen. But
then, I saw him... the creature (if you could
call him that) appeared from the bushes. Please...
dear reader, do not judge him! He was starving
and suffering from God knows what else. How 
has he lived for so long? I wondered. 


"HEEEYAAAAHH!" he screamed, charging me
from the forestry. His spear downed Blitzer 
immediately without even a whimper. I fell to the
ground hitting my head. As I slowly awoke, his
long white beard fluttered in the wind while he 
dug through Blitzer's saddlebag. 

Cautiously, I drew my dagger, standing before
him with a bleeding head. "HALT! THIEF!" I 
screamed. He maniacally laughed at my 
accusation. 

"ME, A THIEF?" The at-the-time unknown bearded man yelled. "THIS LAND HAS TAKEN
EVERYTHING FROM ME, MY PEOPLE, MY 
LAND, MY LIFE!" he lurched at me spear-in-hand.
 I... I... I cannot describe what occurred, but the fight was over with me somehow standing. 


The "creature" was beaten but I knew deep 
down who he was... Leviticus. He must've gone 
mad watching his beloved populace starve.
How else could a man fall to barbarism? I sobbed in that very forest.

Grabbing what remained of my dear elk I realized
something... the farmer was right... I am an uppity
burgher with something to prove! Already I had
it all in Westwald... a warm home, a writing 
career... why risk it all for some vein expedition
to the north? 

Well... I had paid my price. My dear Blitzer was
dead- and somehow... I don't blame the killer. I
commenced my long ashamed path home on foot,
passing by text crudely drawn on the gravel
path, "There is no Perch in Perch Point."

(Bound Stories Printing Press, operated by myworld8, Barony of
Westwald),

Written by Stuvals
(Master Tailor & Diplomat,
Barony of Westwald)

attrs.text:
by Stuvals, Master Tailor & Diplomat of the Barony of Westwald

Lost... where have I gone? Trees tower around me, dark and all foreign. Oddly, I can't even recall how or why I've found myself in this mysterious and uncharted forest.

Suddenly, out of the corner of my spectacles, I spot a glowing... bright, and seemingly unworldly void. No, this is no temporal portal. It's purple, stinking... rotting. A horrifying sight. A man steps out whom identifies himself as Jonas.

His face is half skeleton while the other is putrid beyond recognition. Blood and green foam gushes out his mouth. I'm frozen in place. Many sights I have seen but none akin to this!


"YOU HATH COMMITTED GREAT SINS!" the rotting, standing, and talking Jonas bellows. He pauses, staring. "JUST AS I" saying as his withered arms grab me, tossing me into the great disgusting void with him.

Awaking... seemingly sometime later with a shock. I appear to be in some other realm, a realm of which us seraphim have yet to truly grasp. I'm surrounded by other men. Some young. Others old. All dead. Each bearing great wounds. One man wears a nametag saying "VAK STORE EMPLOYEE #61".

The same recognizable voice of Jonas booms, "WELCOME TO THE LAND OF THE DOOMED!" ending it with a maniacal cackle. "Here is where YOU... MAY ONE DAY LIVE!" 


"Am I dead?" I ask with a hurried panic.

Jonas responds. "DO YOU NOT LISTEN TO ME?" flakes of his decayed skin land on my buckled shoes. "I SAID... ONE DAY, NOT NOW! No, I must showcase this world to your eyes so that YOU... yes you, may spread the word. ONLY THEN CAN YOU BE SAVED... FROM THIS!"

He takes hold of me once more, throwing me down some sort of cascading staircase... my body slams into muddy ground. When I arise... I cannot believe the sight...

A mechanical-esque figure stands towering above blazing infernos of rings. Sometimes dancing, sometimes yelping. Contorted music plays. All terrifying. Thousands of souls sit in torture below.

CIRCLE I: POOR HOSPITALITY

Jonas grabs my head, ripping off my toupée. The fake hair flaps in the wind behind us. "DO YOU SEE?" Men, whose bodies appear starved to death, knock rapidly upon doors. Each damned person has their own one assigned.

"FOR ETERNITY... THEY ARE FORCED TO FEEL STARVATION AND THIRST... ENDLESSLY SEEKING THE AID OF THEIR FELLOW MAN- BUT NO HELP SHALL COME!" He pauses, continuing. "THEY HAVE ALLOWED TRAVELERS TO PASS THEIR HOMES WITHOUT GREETING THEM AND REFUSED TO PROVIDE FOOD TO THE NEEDY."

With his skeletal foot, he kicks me down further.


CIRCLE II: PRICE GAUGING

After standing me up himself, Jonas screams, "ONE OF DAVE'S FAVORITE PRISONERS!" The clanks of thousands of pickaxes are heard. Its sound is so loud, so deafening that it feels as if my eardrums are about to explode.

"THEY MUST FOREVER MINE BROWN COAL ALL TO FUEL THE INFERNO. THE FIRE DOESN'T JUST BLAZE NATURALLY..." Jonas somehow yells over the noise.

"But what have they done to deserve this fate?" I scream in complete panic.

"THESE MEN AND THEIR ILK HAVE SET THEIR PRICES FAR HIGHER THAN THE TRUE VALUE OF THEIR COMMODITIES ON THE MARKET!" 

CIRCLE III: BOMB GRIEFERS

In the fright I was knocked unconscious. Awaking, once more another pitiful sight sprawled out more deafening noise. This time explosions and shrieks. The men pinned to this fate spoke Russian amongst themselves before the next bomb went off. They were tied to their own individual posts with a device strapped to their ears.

"THIS MEN HAVE DEFACED BOTH THE LAND'S NATURAL BEAUTY... AND INNOCENT HOMES!" Jonas shrieks, suddenly right next to me. "THEY HAVE BUILT WEAPONS OF WAR AND USED THEM, UNFAIRLY, AGAINST THEIR COMMON MAN!" The noise went off next to their heads every thirty seconds seemingly.


CIRCLE IV: CHAT ADVERTISERS

"Join New Constantinople today!" a man says, his mouth permanently turned into a smile. "Join New Constantinople today!" he repeats.

"What... what is this?" I ask after being flown into this new, odd fiery circle by Jonas.

A sign bearing "NEW CONSTANTINOPLE" is shown in a never-ending slideshow to hundreds of people strapped into chairs.

"THE MEN DOOMED HERE ARE ONLY ABLE TO UTTER THEIR OWN UNPROMPTED, NOT ASKED FOR CHAT ADVERTISEMENTS. SLOWLY... OVER THE YEARS, THEY GO INSANE."


CIRCLE V: ANIMAL SLAYERS

Jonas this time merely walks me to the next circle. My newly bald head without its false layering sweats in the oven which is Dave's Inferno.

"THESE ARE THE ANIMAL SLAYERS!" Dave gasps.

My mind races. "Hunting for food is a sin?" I ask, attempting to sound collected.

"NO! KILLING WOLVES, BOARS, ELK, AND OTHERS IN PITS WHOM PLAYERS CLEARLY WISH TO BREED IS!"

Men are seen endlessly fighting natural beasts in unceasing cycles without armor or weaponry.


Thunderous thuds creep toward Jonas and I. "Now... my job has been done," he says, disappearing before my very eyes. Only a piece of his flesh remains on the ground. The noise comes closer. I glance back to the hundreds of men all clamoring to stave off wolves before now in front of me is a sight I hardly dare to put to paper...

"You... Stuvals," a creature so large that its mere breath almost causes my body to fly backwards. The smell of its mouth is foul. The mechanical... humanoid entity appears from the vast clouds of darkness it towers over, crouching before me. I have to tilt my head up vertically just to see its "face".

In utter shock I can only answer a scared, "Yes?"
 

CIRCLE VI: FRAUD CURRENCY OWNERS

This entity, which can only be Dave itself, grabs me in this palm of its hand, wafting me over a newfound horrific sight.

Few people endure this fate... but those who do... God save them. Men are frozen solid in blocks, forced to watch screens of their crypto-esque stocks drop lower and lower for eternity.

"THOSE WHO PROMOTE ONLINE CURRENCIES, ON WEBSITES... DWELL HERE!" Dave says, his voice calm but ridiculously loud. "THEIR PEGGED CURRENCIES ARE LIED ABOUT, THEY ARE FREE TO RUGPULL, AND IT'S NOT ABOUT ANYTHING BUT GREED. THIS SIN CAUSES THEIR PLACEMENT HERE."

As I stand upon Dave's hand. I dare to look upwards and ask. "But how is this worse than any other fate... if it is... I assume... the worst?"

"THE FEAR OF LOST PROFITS, OF ONLINE ECONOMIC FAILURE DRIVES THEM MAD... AND WHEN THEY ARE DRIVEN INSANE... I MERELY REVERT THEIR MINDS TO NORMAL AND RESUME THE NEVER-ENDING PUNISHMENT!" he screams to justify his cause.

Having no more of me, I'm flung upwards. It feels as if for hours I screamed, my body traversing thousands of miles in-air. "While starving as a new player I did indeed raid someone's boar pit!" I yelp. "Maybe I did sell purple heart logs for far more than they're worth!" adding on. Finally, I fly through the same purplish void I entered.


Home! At last! Arising from my stupor upon marbled floors... in a puddle of my filth, I glance around. A suction noise erupts from the portal closing. In being shot out from the void I knocked down numerous of my beloved mannequins... my carefully tailored clothes falling with them.

However the excitement quickly wears off. I have sinned. Such has been admitted in my flight from Dave's toss. My first ambition for my own salvation is to pen this work, so that all shall know of what awaits them if they commit these printed ills!







Published by B.S. Publishing 
(Bound Stories Printing Press, operated by myworld8, Barony of
Westwald),

Written by Stuvals
(Master Tailor & Diplomat,
Barony of Westwald)

Many older animals that were effected were brought back from whatever plane they were sent to. Strangely enough, animals that were never stricken with Wipeall were also summoned back... alongside their unaffected counterparts. While the animals who were once missing returned to their normal state of existing, the newly effected animals caught a terrible case of Temporal Fever; existing in two separate locations at once with their modern selves and their "May 3rd" selves fighting for their very presence in reality. My beloved elk, Tank, was one of the victims. The morning I woke up after the successful ritual summoning, I found Tank was safely where I had last seen him. In my crop garden, left there as a treat once word of spread of attempts to rewind time itself were likely (time, in fact, was never rewound). All seemed well and good, until I checked within his stable. He was also there. Curious, I went to take him for a ride from the stable, only to find myself suddenly atop him in the location of his other self in the garden. Something was very wrong. Thinking I was now on his garden self, I attempted instead to guide this version to the stable, using some stacked boards as an easy step to hop the fence. Big mistake. We suddenly soared Southeast over the fence, hitting the charcoal factory, then straight upwards, then Southeast again, upwards to a height of 632 meters and southwards by 655 before we landed. While Tank had once again saved me from any harm, he had sustained fatal injuries. I rushed to try and get the bandages from his saddlebag, only to find they were not there. The saddlebags themselves were not even there. That's when I noticed the blanket. The blanket he was wearing was the survivor quilt. The one he was wearing in the past. This was not the one from the garden. This was the one summoned back to the stable. I dubbed this his "Maythird" self. Panicked on what would happen to his Wipeall counterpart (the name I dubbed his more modern self) if Maythird died, I sprinted home on foot to get bandages. When I returned, I saw Wipeall Tank, standing still in the garden, fully healthy. I could not access the contents of his saddlebag either, but they existed. I grabbed bandages from a stash and sprinted back to Maythird, frantically applying bandages. The thought occured to bandage his Wipeall self as well for good measure, so I returned to do so, and gathered supplies to safely secure the one who had mistaken himself for a pegasus. I removed his tack at this time, unknowingly setting in place what may have started to link the two back together. It was clear by this point that I had one goal. All other jobs were to be put on hold to take care of the two not-so-coexisting variations of my elk, dubbed Maythird and Wipeall Tank. First I attempted to remove their gear, starting with Maythird's. When I got to Wipeall's gear, it seemed rather... partially existing. The sturdy saddlebags could not come off. I removed the commoner blanket, only to find it went back to him when I placed it in a chest. He also seemed to be strangely stationary. With what had just happened with Maythird, I wished not to risk Wipeall changing elevation. My garden was to be repurposed into his recovery pen. It was time to start paying attention to other seraphs with elk suffering the same ailment. One said their elk recovered when far away from his other self. At first, Wipeall Tank still struggled, but after a few hours with Maythird in his landing site, Wipeall seemed to gain a small amount of clarity. It did not feel like enough to move him out of recovery. I struggled to place Maythird's tack and medallion back on, but easily did so on Wipeall. I kept them identical, save for one thing. A linen blanket for Wipeall. Cheap, expendable, but comfortable. As for Maythird, I got his tack back on eventually, and in a say or so he seemed to be feeling stable. Another seraph claimed their separation to be the cure, that being close cause both of them trauma, and while this looked to be the truth, my gut was saying otherwise. Slowly, but carefully, I guided Maythird back home. Sure enough, when he got close to Wipeall, another temporal anomaly happened. We got blinked into the garden. They were both blinking, but there. Somehow this felt like the right course of action. Several days passed. I got in contact with a seraph with young bucks unaffected by the recent events, and purchased one to aid in travel while Tank was suffering from temporal fever. There seemed to be some pigs around the farm with the fever as well, so I started searching for them and their counterparts, successfully identifying and enclosing 2 pairs; a sow and a boar. With the pigs at hand, I started with a burning question. What happens if one dies? The effected entities are blinking between two locations as they quarrel on who exists. If one dies, does the other stabilise, or cease to exist as well? I grabbed a spear, hesitant to try such a brutal test. Until I remembered how often those damn pigs went after my own life. I killed the sow. She was still fighting on who existed as she lay dead. Both were as such, but harvesting either was impossible as they were blinking too fast. So I waited until her body decomposed, at the location I killed her. When this happened, her other self "won", but at a terrible price. The remaining clone remained standing in place, unmoving, seemingly lobotomised. Never sleeping. Never sitting. No reaction to my presence nor roughhousing. Though I am unconvinced this was caused by the death of her other. Because she wasn't the only one. As I looked around the land, several blinking animals now had two very distinct variations. One that seemed to be living normally, or as normally as they could, and one that was seemingly just a shell. I went to Tank's recovery pen. Held my breath, and attempted to give Wipeall a startle, who seemed to be the lifeless one by now. No reaction. I did the same to Maythird. Reaction! He ran around from the tap. This seems to be a development in the temporal fever. The two also seem to be slightly more linked now, as altering the gear on one alters the gear on the other. With this development, Tank, in both his times, has the linen blanket. His commoner blanket and sturdy saddlebags seem to be lost forever to the temporal anomaly, while his old survivor blanket has duplicated. I carry on, finding and marking locations of other effected animals. Given a few more days, they progress slightly further, excepting the sow. The shells now are sharing movements with their free-roaming selves, despite still standing in place. It feels as though time is recovering. And then - time stops. For us all. Briefly. In the void of nonexistence as we all wait, there is much noise made about the world's stability. When time starts up again, I open my eyes, rise up, and check on the two Tanks. Or rather, the ONE Tank! He seemed dazed at first. Standing still, unwilling to move after I dismounted his saddle. I gave him another small startle, and he springs into action, back to normal. At long last, his temporal fever seems to be gone. I'm still employing the younger buck for now on journeys involving Translocators; Tank could use his rest. He's survived, and recovered from, what has been by far the most powerful temporal event we've ever seen.

BOAT DESIGN FLAWS ENDANGER CREWS

Heliastes, WSJ Editor-in-Chief

   It was calm seas and clear skies, an typical seafaring day on the Southeastern Oceans for MangoKingOfFruit, known affectionately as "The Mange" to their friends. But after MangoKingOfFruit engaged the rudder for a minor course correction, everything quickly changed. "I remember the ship violently rolling to the right, then immediately rolling back over to the left, then yawing almost 90 degrees and throwing me into the mast. I don't remember anything after that," said MangoKingOfFruit, speaking from the Throughway Rehabilitation Facility. MangoKingOfFruit had been rescued from a deserted island nearly 120 days after the incident at sea. "I woke up, looked around, and saw that I was on a peridotite sand beach with a few trees. I walked about 50 steps through the trees and found nothing but ocean; I then realized I was in huge trouble." MangoKingOfFruit was trapped on a sandbar island no larger than Kralmir's dirt hut.
   "I survived on rainwater dripping from the tree leaves, collecting it in my boots for the dry season," explained MangoKingOfFruit. "I then fashioned a crude spear from the contents of a washed-up aged crate and spear-fished for food. I sifted sand everyday until I got enough copper nuggets to hammer a few nails together with some rocks, then fashioned a bamboo raft and took off to the west." MangoKingOfFruit was found adrift by a passing ship weeks after leaving the island, their supplies depleted and nearly dead of sun exposure and thirst. "I don't think they would have lasted another day if we hadn't found them," said DuStPaInFuL, who was manning their dredging boat for the Southeast Oceans Canal project when they spotted the raft.
TOPS Investigation and Safety Management (TISM) launched an investigation into the mishap at sea and found that MangoKingOfFruit's ship had suffered an increasingly common mechanical failure. "Our investigation found that the ship suffered a rudder hardover event," said SirWelshie, lead investigator. "The rudder turns beyond it's mechanical limits and jams, leading to excessive hydrodynamic forces that can breakup the ship." Manufacturers have known about this design deficiency for years but have yet to take steps to address the issue. "In our view, addressing an design issue that affects less than one in a thousand ship journeys does not pass the muster of a cost-benefit analysis," said RubyShield, owner of the shipping conglomerate Brillig Marine Transport. "We encourage pilots to review their manuals and ensure that all rudder inputs are properly executed."

BOAT DESIGN FLAWS ENDANGER CREWS

Heliastes, WSJ Editor-in-Chief

   It was calm seas and clear skies, an typical seafaring day on the Southeastern Oceans for MangoKingOfFruit, known affectionately as "The Mange" to their friends. But after MangoKingOfFruit engaged the rudder for a minor course correction, everything quickly changed. "I remember the ship violently rolling to the right, then immediately rolling back over to the left, then yawing almost 90 degrees and throwing me into the mast. I don't remember anything after that," said MangoKingOfFruit, speaking from the Throughway Rehabilitation Facility. MangoKingOfFruit had been rescued from a deserted island nearly 120 days after the incident at sea. "I woke up, looked around, and saw that I was on a peridotite sand beach with a few trees. I walked about 50 steps through the trees and found nothing but ocean; I then realized I was in huge trouble." MangoKingOfFruit was trapped on a sandbar island no larger than Kralmir's dirt hut.
   "I survived on rainwater dripping from the tree leaves, collecting it in my boots for the dry season," explained MangoKingOfFruit. "I then fashioned a crude spear from the contents of a washed-up aged crate and spear-fished for food. I sifted sand everyday until I got enough copper nuggets to hammer a few nails together with some rocks, then fashioned a bamboo raft and took off to the west." MangoKingOfFruit was found adrift by a passing ship weeks after leaving the island, their supplies depleted and nearly dead of sun exposure and thirst. "I don't think they would have lasted another day if we hadn't found them," said DuStPaInFuL, who was manning their dredging boat for the Southeast Oceans Canal project when they spotted the raft.
TOPS Investigation and Safety Management (TISM) launched an investigation into the mishap at sea and found that MangoKingOfFruit's ship had suffered an increasingly common mechanical failure. "Our investigation found that the ship suffered a rudder hardover event," said SirWelshie, lead investigator. "The rudder turns beyond it's mechanical limits and jams, leading to excessive hydrodynamic forces that can breakup the ship." Manufacturers have known about this design deficiency for years but have yet to take steps to address the issue. "In our view, addressing an design issue that affects less than one in a thousand ship journeys does not pass the muster of a cost-benefit analysis," said RubyShield, owner of the shipping conglomerate Brillig Marine Transport. "We encourage pilots to review their manuals and ensure that all rudder inputs are properly executed."
